title: Absolute values decrease coordinate influence
statement: For every dimension $n\ge0$, real-valued function $h$ on $\{0,1\}^n$, and coordinate $i\in[n]$, the influence of $i$ on the pointwise absolute value $|h|$ is at most its influence on $h$: $\mathrm{Inf}_i[|h|]\le \mathrm{Inf}_i[h]$.
replaced: Let $n\ge0$ and equip $\{0,1\}^n$ with its uniform probability measure; write $\mathbb E$ for uniform expectation. Write $x^{\{i\}}$ for $x$ with bit $i$ flipped, $I_i(h)=\mathbb E[(h(x)-h(x^{\{i\}}))^2]/4$, and $I(h)=\sum_i I_i(h)$. For every real function $h$ on the cube and coordinate $i\in[n]$, $I_i(|h|)\le I_i(h)$.
